title: Client Development & Best Practices 🚀
content: Mastering the AMPS SDKs
Optimizing for Low Latency
Building Resilient Applications
speakerNotes: Welcome to Module 10. Today we dive into how to build world-class applications using AMPS SDKs and how to squeeze every bit of performance out of your OS and hardware.

title: AMPS Client SDKs: Multi-language Support 🌍
content: Native SDKs for: Java, C#, C++, Python, Go, and JavaScript.
Consistency across languages: Unified API design.
High performance: Optimized for the specific runtime (e.g., Zero-copy in C++).
Platform support: Linux, Windows, macOS, and Cloud environments.
speakerNotes: AMPS supports all major enterprise languages. Each SDK is optimized for its specific environment while maintaining a consistent programming model across the board.

title: Core Interfaces: Message & Command 🛠️
content: **Command**: The 'verbs' of AMPS (Subscribe, Publish, SOW, Delta).
**Message**: The 'nouns' containing payload and metadata (Topic, SOW Key, Bookmark).
Metadata access: Efficiently retrieve header info without full payload parsing.
Payload flexibility: Support for JSON, FIX, BFlat, Protobuf, and Binary.
speakerNotes: Every interaction in AMPS revolves around these two interfaces. Commands go to the server; Messages come back.

title: Programming Pattern: Asynchronous Callbacks 🔄
content: Don't block the main thread! 🛑
Message Handlers: Register a function/method to handle incoming data.
Concurrency: AMPS clients often use background threads for network I/O.
Thread Safety: Ensure your handler logic is thread-safe or hands off to a worker queue.
mermaid:
graph LR
  A[Network Thread] -- Message --> B{Message Handler}
  B -- Process --> C[App Logic]
  B -- Queue --> D[Worker Thread Pool]
speakerNotes: Asynchronous processing is the key to maintaining high throughput and low latency. Use a handler to receive messages and immediately return control to the SDK.

title: Exception Handling & Error Recovery 🛡️
content: Connection Errors: Network drops, timeouts, and refused connections.
Entitlement Errors: Unauthorized access to topics or commands.
Protocol Errors: Invalid filters or malformed messages.
Best Practice: Implement an Exception Listener to catch background errors.
speakerNotes: In a distributed system, things fail. Your code must be ready to catch exceptions not just in the main loop, but in background listeners as well.

title: High Availability: HAClient & Reconnection 🔄
content: **HAClient**: Wrapper that manages multiple server URIs.
Automatic Reconnection: Loops through servers until one is available.
State Management: Resubscribes to active topics upon reconnection.
Transparency: The application continues to function during the failover.
mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as HAClient
  participant S1 as Primary Server
  participant S2 as Backup Server
  C->>S1: Connect & Subscribe
  Note over S1: Server Fails 💥
  C->>C: Detect Disconnect
  C->>S2: Reconnect
  C->>S2: Resubscribe with Bookmark
  S2-->>C: Catch-up Messages
speakerNotes: The HAClient is the 'Easy Button' for high availability. It handles the complexity of finding a live server and resuming your exact state using bookmarks.

title: Bookmark Subscriptions for Data Integrity ✅
content: Never miss a message! 📉
Bookmarks: Unique IDs for every message in the transaction log.
Bookmark Stores: Local file or memory to track 'last seen' messages.
Resume: On restart, the client asks for data starting 'after' the last bookmark.
speakerNotes: Combine the HAClient with a Bookmark Store to create a 'gapless' subscription that survives both network drops and application restarts.

title: Performance Tuning: CPU Pinning & NUMA 🧠
content: **CPU Pinning**: Bind AMPS threads to specific physical cores.
**NUMA**: Non-Uniform Memory Access awareness.
Minimize context switches: Keep threads on their assigned cores.
Memory Locality: Access memory on the same socket as the CPU.
speakerNotes: On modern multi-socket servers, the distance between the CPU and memory matters. AMPS is NUMA-aware, and you should ensure your OS configuration respects this.

title: Performance Tuning: Disk I/O (XFS & SSD) 💾
content: Transaction logs need fast sequential writes. ✍️
Use SSD or NVMe for low-latency persistence.
Filesystem: **XFS** is highly recommended for AMPS performance.
Avoid NFS for primary logs: Latency and locking issues are common.
speakerNotes: Disk latency is the most common bottleneck for persistent messaging. Use local fast storage and the XFS filesystem for the best results.

title: OS Tuning: Transparent Huge Pages (THP) 📄
content: The Problem: THP can cause 'stalls' during memory allocation.
The Solution: **Disable THP** for AMPS workloads.
Why? Large, unpredictable latency spikes are unacceptable for trading apps.
Command: `echo never > /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled`
speakerNotes: Transparent Huge Pages are great for some apps, but for low-latency messaging, they introduce jitter. Disable them to ensure consistent performance.

title: OS Tuning: TCP Settings for Low Latency ⚡
content: `TCP_NODELAY`: Disable Nagle's algorithm to send small packets immediately.
`SO_RCVBUF` / `SO_SNDBUF`: Tune buffer sizes for high-throughput pipes.
Interrupt Coalescing: Adjust NIC settings to process packets faster.
Bypass the stack? Consider Kernel Bypass (Solarflare/Mellanox) for ultra-low latency.
speakerNotes: Standard TCP settings are for throughput, not latency. We need to tune the stack to ensure every message is delivered as fast as the wire allows.

title: Threading Models: Client-side Parallelism 🧵
content: Single-threaded handlers: Easy but can be a bottleneck.
Pipeline Processing: One thread for I/O, many for processing.
Lock-free queues: Use Disrupter or similar patterns for inter-thread handoffs.
Goal: Maximize CPU saturation across all available cores.
mermaid:
graph TD
  A[NIC] --> B[SDK Network Thread]
  B --> C[Lock-Free Queue]
  C --> D1[Worker 1]
  C --> D2[Worker 2]
  C --> D3[Worker 3]
speakerNotes: Don't let your business logic slow down your message reception. Use a high-performance threading model to scale your application.

title: Deployment Checklist: Pre-Production 📋
content: ✅ Hardware: Verified NUMA and CPU layout.
✅ OS: THP disabled, TCP tuned, XFS mounted.
✅ AMPS: Replication active, HAClient tested.
✅ Monitoring: Galvanometer and Alerts configured.
✅ Scaling: Load tested with production-like message volumes.
speakerNotes: Before you click 'Go', walk through this checklist. Most production issues are caused by simple configuration misses in the OS or hardware layers.

title: Summary & Best Practices Recap ✨
content: Use the right SDK and the HAClient for resilience. 🛡️
Optimize your code with async patterns and bookmark stores. 🔄
Tune your hardware and OS for the microsecond level. ⏱️
Monitor everything! 📊
speakerNotes: We've covered a lot today. Remember: AMPS is fast, but your application is only as fast as its slowest component. Tune every layer!
